title: Lock a free-rolling utility cart in place: press both locking casters' brake tabs fully down so it no longer rolls
keywords: press a brake tab past its latch
instruction: Lock the cart in place: press down the brake tabs on both of its locking wheels until each locks, then move both hands clear.
context: A rolling cart, stand or trolley is locked before it is loaded or worked at, by pressing down the brake tab on each of its locking wheels, a step most people know from utility carts, cribs, office equipment and hospital beds. For a robot the press is the hard part: the tab is small and low, on the caster just in front of the cart's bottom shelf; only a tab pressed past its latch locks, while one pressed part way springs back and leaves the wheel free; and each press pushes the free cart forward on its wheels. The cart here is a stock 3-tier metal utility cart at its real size, 15.5 x 11 x 28.25 in and 7.85 lb, with two locking casters. It stands on the table, which stands for the floor, because the robot's arms can't reach floor level, and a hand presses each tab where a person would use a foot; these two stagings are the only changes from real use. Success is judged by effect: once locked, the cart no longer rolls when pushed.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases at (0, +30.5) and (0, -30.5), at the near edge of the station table (110 x 130 cm top, 75 cm high). Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Staging: the cart stands on the table top, which stands for the floor. Cart: Mind Reader LIDCART3T-BLK 3-tier metal utility cart, 15.5 x 11 x 28.25 in (39.4 x 27.9 x 71.8 cm), 3.56 kg, black powder-coated steel: four round corner posts about 19 mm across (assumed), their outsides on the cart's outline; a perforated bottom shelf, a tray with a 2.5 cm lip, its top 10 cm up (design); a tier of two drawers side by side, 33 to 47 cm up; a covered compartment at the top, 58.5 to 71.8 cm up; drawers and compartment empty. It stands with its length along y, centred at (45, 0): x 31.05 to 58.95, y -19.7 to 19.7. Casters: four swivel casters 72 mm high overall with 50 mm wheels (assumed, 40 to 65 mm), each swivel axis 2.5 cm in from its corner: the two locking ones near the robot at (33.55, +/-17.2), the two plain ones at (56.45, +/-17.2); every wheel trails 2 cm behind its swivel axis, all four trailing straight toward +x at the start, so that the brake tabs face the robot. Brakes, assumed with ranges as the listing gives no figure: each locking caster is a total lock (wheel and swivel), worked by a red tab (nylon, assumed) 20 mm wide on its fork that stands out toward the robot from 0.8 to 4.5 cm in front of the swivel axis: its pressed end at x 29.05, 2 cm in front of the shelf's front edge, its top 6.5 cm up, open above. It latches down once pressed 7 mm of its 8 mm travel (travel 5 to 12 mm on such casters), at about 9 N (6 to 15 N; 10 N at full travel), and stays down; pressed less, it springs back up and the caster stays free. If the real cart's casters lock only the wheel, a trial fits total-lock casters of the same size. Rolling resistance: the free cart starts rolling at about 2.5 N (1 to 4 N); swivel friction 0.03 N m; the wheels' rubber tread on the wood table top, friction 0.8 (0.7 sliding). A real trial stands the cart on the station table's smooth hard top, with stops along the table's edges so a free cart cannot roll or topple off, and measures the free cart's rolling force with the spring gauge first. Both grippers start open at their rest pose, TCPs at (32.3, +/-30.5), 26 cm up. Reset: lift both tabs to unlock, set all four wheels trailing straight toward +x and the cart's post feet back on their tape marks.
scoring: By effect, with tape marks on the table top at the feet of the four corner posts, the video, a ruler and a spring gauge. The cart's position is its middle, the mean of its four post feet against their marks, so a turn in place is not a move. Score 0 if the cart tips more than 10 degrees or lifts 2 cm off the table (the video), or if its middle moves more than 5 cm from its start outside the test pushes (a move the pushes caused still counts once they end). Otherwise the rungs are cumulative: 0.25 with one locking caster's tab latched down (it stays down when let go: look and touch); 0.5 with both; 0.75 with both and the cart's middle never more than 2 cm from its start outside the test pushes; 1.0 with that and then, with every fingertip and arm joint of both arms at least 3 cm from the cart (the video), a push along +x at the middle of the bottom shelf's front edge, 10 cm up, raised to 8 N over half a second and held 1 s, and then the same along +y at the right front post's outside, 10 cm up, the two together moving the bottom shelf's front-edge middle, its two front corners and its back right corner each less than 5 mm (applied by the scorer in simulation and by a spring gauge in a real trial; ruler against the marks), and the cart then standing still for 1 s with the hands still clear (no movement seen in the video; within 1 mm in simulation). 8 N is twice the top of the free cart's assumed rolling resistance, so the push tells a locked cart from a free one. A tab only part way down (under 7 mm), with its caster still free, does not count; in simulation a tab counts only if a fingertip is within 3 cm of its top line while it is past the latch. If a hand comes back within 3 cm during the pushes, they start again once it is clear.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on the GPU. Each wheel meets the floor as a ball of its radius with a 5 mm contact patch, a round tread alike at every angle. Rolling and swivel resistance are dry friction held by drives (2.5 N starts the free cart rolling). The tab is a sprung slide (8 mm, 9 N at the 7 mm latch); the latch and the total lock are coded: stiff drives hold wheel and swivel. Tab, wheel and resistance values are assumed; a real trial measures them. Table for floor; hand for foot.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 in 2,400 steps (it pressed neither tab); demo: 1.0
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials: lift both tabs to unlock, set all four wheels trailing straight toward +x, and put the cart back on its tape marks.
